text:
Riley (Design): Quick check on a compact threshold row for SLO alerts. Idea: collapse label + value + preview into a single line with an expandable chevron. Wire: https://figma.redwood/compact-threshold. Is this readable / accessible?

Omar (Eng): Compact row is nice for density. Implementation risk: inline validation messages need space. If we expand in-place, focus management gets tricky.

Zoe (A11y): For screen readers, each collapsed row needs an accessible name and `aria-expanded` on the button. When expanded, move focus to the first input. Use `aria-controls` to point to detail panel.

Riley (Design): Good. We'll add `aria-expanded` and ensure the chevron is a real button. Visual design: keep contrast high for the inline preview text so it passes AA in both themes.

Carlos (Product): Copy thought: preview currently says "Notify when > 10 errors". Suggest: "Will notify when error count > 10 in a 5m window". Explicit window avoids confusion.

Tess (PM): Also: if suppression is active for this alert, show a muted badge in the row: "Suppressed until Mar 24 14:00 (UTC)". Clicking it should open suppression details.

Omar (Eng): Backend note: include suppression metadata in the list response to avoid extra calls. Also pagination could hide suppressed items; ensure badges appear even when row is virtualized.

Zoe (A11y): For the suppressed badge, include `role=img` and `aria-label` like "Suppressed until March 24th, 2026, 14:00 UTC". Also ensure color isn't the only indicator; add a muted icon.

Riley (Design): On mobile, we'll collapse details under the chevron; preview text truncated with ellipsis and full preview accessible via `aria-label`.

docs-bot: Heads up: update docs section "Alert list compact mode" after design is final.

Carlos (Product): Timeline: finalize copy + ARIA examples by tomorrow. Thanks team!"
